tower.title: Control Tower
tower.lead: Every headline here drills to the records underneath it.
tower.productionNote: Expected and actual harvest by crop and window.
tower.pueNote: Requests by status, with the catalogue value they represent.
tower.marketNote: Open demand against supply that is still available.
tower.qualityNote: How much of what has been recorded has been checked.
tower.plantedAreaNote: The sum of cycle areas. Intercropping means several cycles share a plot, so this can exceed the village’s hectares. It is not land area.
tower.indicativeValueNote: Indicative catalogue value: price times quantity. Not financed value and not a loan book.
tower.prospectiveNote: Requests submitted or under review. An application, not a load.
tower.approvedNote: Decided yes. Still not measured consumption.
tower.headroomNote: Approved peak against planned capacity. Prospective requests are not on this bar; they are not a load.
tower.simultaneityNote: Applied to the peaks above. Village peak is not the sum of rated power.
tower.neverSummed: Prospective and approved are separate figures and are never added together.
tower.noVillageDetail: The Tower reports on one village at a time.
tower.noDataDetail: This tile fills in as records are created.
tower.noCapacityDetail: A current village_capacity row is needed before energy figures can be shown.

farmer.welcomeBody: This is your own record. Everything here was written by a field officer who visited your farm, and every figure shows where it came from. The tour button in the header (the person icon on a phone) shows you any part of the app whenever you want.
farmer.summaryTitle: What is on file for you
farmer.summaryBody: Your farm, your plots and what you expect to harvest. If something here is wrong, tell your field officer — they are the one who can correct it.
farmer.recordsBody: Each record carries a badge saying who recorded it and whether an officer has verified it. Unverified does not mean wrong; it means nobody has checked it yet.
farmer.equipmentBody: Browse what is available and what it would cost to run. Every price here is indicative — it is a guide, not a quotation, and nothing is ordered from this screen.
farmer.requestsBody: Every request you send appears here with its current status, so you can see whether it is waiting, under review, approved or turned down — and why.
farmer.opportunitiesBody: An opportunity is a buyer looking for a crop, matched to what your village expects to harvest. It is not a sale, a delivery or a payment — nothing is owed either way.
farmer.surveysTitle: Surveys, and the incentive for answering
farmer.surveysBody: Answer a survey and your household receives a fixed cash incentive, once per survey. You get a voucher code; show it at the Ruaha office to collect the cash. The number on this tab is how many surveys are waiting for you.

officer.welcomeBody: This is the field officer's surface. You register farmers, verify what you recorded, and hand over survey incentives. The tour button in the header (the person icon on a phone) shows you any part of it again whenever you want.
officer.outstandingBody: Everything you record starts unverified. This counts what is waiting for you. Verify only what you have seen yourself — it cannot be undone.
officer.registerBody: Six groups — person, household, farm, plot, crop cycle, expected harvest — created together in a single step. These chips show which groups you have filled in.
officer.oneSubmitBody: Press this once. If the signal drops the form stays saved on this phone, and pressing it again after a failure replays the same registration rather than creating a second farmer.
officer.peopleBody: Search by name or phone, or filter by whether records are verified. Opening a person shows every record attached to them and who recorded each one.
officer.verifyBody: Everything awaiting verification, in one list. Verifying says you have seen the record yourself. There is no way to un-verify, so leave anything you are unsure of.
officer.redeemBody: Scan the farmer's voucher, check their ID and hand over the cash. You cannot redeem a voucher for a household you registered or verified, and some vouchers are held for ops to redeem in person. Every scan is recorded with your name.

ops.welcomeBody: This is the programme surface: requests, buyer demand, surveys and the Control Tower. The tour button in the header lets you pick any part of it to be shown at any time.
ops.queueBody: Each tile counts one queue and opens it. They are counts of work, not performance figures.
ops.requestsBody: Every equipment request, filterable by status and village. Opening one shows the farmer's own words, the energy estimate and the decision controls.
ops.demandBody: What buyers are asking for, and how much of it a village could cover. Prices are indicative throughout. Creating an opportunity records a match — it is not a sale.
ops.towerBody: Production, energy, market and data quality for one village. Every figure is read from the database and drills down to the record it came from.
ops.towerVillageBody: The Tower is always about one village. Capacity here is planned and always shown with its basis — never measured — and prospective and approved demand are separate figures that are never added together.
ops.surveysBody: Admin writes and publishes surveys here. Each household answers once and collects a fixed cash incentive at the office. You see who answered, which vouchers are collected, and the full trail of names behind each one; Redemptions totals the cash handed over per officer per day.
